content.text:
Start working on Linear ticket eng-2244 by fetching its details and creating a dedicated git worktree.

## Steps

### 1. Validate input
- `eng-2244` should be a Linear ticket ID like `ENG-1271`. If missing or malformed, ask the user.

### 2. Fetch ticket details from Linear
- Use `mcp__linear-server__get_issue` with the issue ID `eng-2244`
- Extract: title, description, and `branchName` (Linear provides this)
- If the Linear tool is unavailable, ask the user for a branch name manually

### 3. Determine branch name
- Use the `branchName` field from Linear if available (it's already formatted correctly)
- Otherwise derive it: lowercase the ticket ID + hyphenated slug of the title
  - Example: `ENG-1271 Implement filter search` → `eng-1271-implement-filter-search`
  - Strip special characters, replace spaces with hyphens, truncate to ~60 chars

### 4. Create git worktree
Run these from the repo root (the main working directory, not an existing worktree):

```bash
# Fetch latest main so the worktree starts from up-to-date origin/main
git fetch origin main

# Check if branch already exists
git branch --list <branch-name>

# Check if worktree already exists
git worktree list | grep <branch-name>
```

- **If worktree already exists**: skip to step 5, just `cd` into `.claude/worktrees/<branch-name>`
- **If branch does NOT exist**: `git worktree add -b <branch-name> .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> origin/main`
- **If branch already exists but no worktree**: reset the branch to `origin/main` first, then add the worktree:
  ```bash
  git branch -f <branch-name> origin/main
  git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> <branch-name>
  ```

### 5. Enter the worktree
**Do NOT use the `EnterWorktree` tool** — it always creates a brand-new worktree and will duplicate the one you just created.

Instead, use `cd` to switch into the worktree directory:
```bash
cd .claude/worktrees/<branch-name>
```

All subsequent commands should run from this path.

### 6. Install dependencies and set up the worktree
After entering the worktree, run the following to bootstrap the environment:

```bash
pnpm install
```

This is required because worktrees share git objects but each needs its own `node_modules`.

### 6b. Copy .env files from the main repo into the worktree
`.env` files are gitignored, so each worktree needs its own copies. After `pnpm install`, copy all `.env` files (excluding `.env.example` files) from the main repo root into the matching relative paths in the worktree.

The main repo root is the working directory you were in before entering the worktree (e.g. `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph`).

Run:
```bash
# From the main repo root, find all .env files (not .env.example) and copy them into the worktree
find . -name ".env*" \
  -not -name ".env.example" \
  -not -path "./.git/*" \
  -not -path "./node_modules/*" \
  -not -path "./.claude/worktrees/*" \
  | while read f; do
      dest=".claude/worktrees/<branch-name>/$f"
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
      cp "$f" "$dest"
    done
```

Report which files were copied so the user can confirm.

The copied `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH` points at the main checkout's vault. Step 7 replaces it
with the vault leased to this worktree.

### 6c. Link the shared `dg-*` skills into the worktree

Claude Code only loads skills from `.claude/skills`, but the repo's shared skills live in
`.agents/skills`. Without this step they never load in the worktree: they cannot trigger on
their own descriptions and have no slash command.

Run from the main repo root, substituting the worktree path:

```bash
WT=".claude/worktrees/<branch-name>"
MAIN="$PWD"
mkdir -p "$WT/.claude/skills"
for src in "$MAIN"/.agents/skills/dg-*/; do
  s=$(basename "$src")
  if [ -d "$WT/.agents/skills/$s" ]; then
    # Relative link, so the worktree uses its own branch's copy of the skill.
    ln -sfn "../../.agents/skills/$s" "$WT/.claude/skills/$s"
  else
    # Branch predates the skill; fall back to the main checkout's copy.
    ln -sfn "$MAIN/.agents/skills/$s" "$WT/.claude/skills/$s"
  fi
done
ls -l "$WT/.claude/skills/"
```

Verify each link resolves before moving on:

```bash
for d in "$WT"/.claude/skills/dg-*; do
  [ -f "$d/SKILL.md" ] || echo "BROKEN: $d"
done
```

These links are gitignored (`.claude/*`), so they are local to this machine and add nothing
to the diff. Use a glob rather than a variable list: zsh does not word-split unquoted
variables, so `for s in $SKILLS` silently iterates once with the whole string.

### 7. Ask the user which app to start
Ask the user which app they want to run in dev mode. Common options:
- **Roam**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=none pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/roam dev`
- **Obsidian**: `node ~/.claude/skills/obsidian-vault/scripts/vault.mjs dev --worktree <worktree>`
  - This leases a free local-db vault and writes `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH` and `SUPABASE_USE_DB` for
    it into `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env`. It then starts the watcher. A later plain `pnpm dev`
    and CDP runs use the same vault. Add `--db production` only if the user asks to test against
    prod (testVault123).
  - For **None**, still run `vault.mjs claim --worktree <worktree>` if the ticket touches
    apps/obsidian, so the `.env` doesn't keep pointing at the main checkout's vault.
  - **Exit 2** means every vault in that pool is taken. Follow the `obsidian-vault` skill: ask the
    user which vault to take over, then rerun with `--take <vault>`. Never pick one yourself.
  - On success, pass the printed `obsidian://open?path=` URL to the user, so they open that vault.
- **None**: just set up the environment without starting a dev server

If the user says Roam, also switch the Roam dev symlink:
```bash
ln -sfn <worktree>/apps/roam/dist ~/roam-ext-dev
```
and remind them to reload the developer extension in Roam.

Run the chosen dev command in the background so the user can continue working.

**Dev server gotchas** (learned the hard way — don't rediscover these):

- The filter flag is `--filter`, not `--F`. Turbo 2.5.6 rejects `--F=roam` outright.
- Prefer `pnpm -C <abs-path> <app> dev` over `turbo dev --filter=<app>`. `turbo dev --filter=roam`
  also runs the `@repo/database#dev` dependency, which requires Docker Desktop plus an explicit
  `SUPABASE_USE_DB`; if Docker isn't running turbo fails the *entire* run even though the app
  itself built fine. Going through `pnpm -C` skips the dependency graph.
- `SUPABASE_USE_DB` must be one of `local | branch | production | none | implicit`
  (see `packages/database/src/dbDotEnv.mjs`). Use `none` for work that doesn't touch the database.
- **Always bake the absolute worktree path into the command.** The Bash tool's cwd resets to the
  main repo between calls, so a backgrounded `pnpm --filter roam dev` with no path silently builds
  the *main repo's* `dist` — not the worktree the symlink points at. `pnpm -C <abs-path>` makes the
  path intrinsic to the command so it can't be dropped.
- After starting, verify before reporting success: confirm the log says `built with 0 errors` **and**
  that `<worktree>/apps/roam/dist` has a fresh mtime. A background task that failed still returns a
  task ID.

### 8. Ingest any saved session context
The branch may have been worked on before (e.g. reset from an existing branch).
Check for recorded session context:

```bash
bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve
```

- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=yes`, **read the `CONTEXT_FILE`** and load it as working context
  (`Next step`, `Open questions`, `Key decisions`, `Dead ends`).
- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=no` or the command errors, continue — this is a fresh start.

### 9. Show context
After setup, display:
- Ticket ID and title
- Branch name you're on
- Brief description from the ticket (if available)
- Which app dev server is running (if any), and for Obsidian, which vault is leased
- That the shared `dg-*` skills are linked and resolving
- If prior session context was found: its `TL;DR` and `Next step`
- A short "ready to work" confirmation
- Remind the user they can run `/checkpoint` to save session context before wrapping up

> **TL;DR** PR 3 of 3, stacked on ENG-2243, and it absorbs ENG-2245 (Duplicate). `Create new` opens a Blueprint dialog with Label and Complement fields and no color. Input is validated against the existing triplets. On submit it calls ENG-2243's `createTripletForPair` and shows two toasts. This PR carries the end-to-end check of ENG-2241.

## Goal / scope agreement
- **Stack:** eng-1955 ← ENG-2242 ← ENG-2243 ← **ENG-2244**. Overview: `AI_sessions/eng-2241-implement-canvas-relation-creation-for-unconfigured-node/plan.md`.
- **"Create new" also just saves a triplet.** The only difference from Add existing is that the label is new.
- **In scope:** the dialog, validation, wiring `onCreateNew`, the toasts, and the end-to-end check of DES-349 Cases 1–3.
- **Out of scope:**
  - a color picker (ENG-2244 says color is automatic and derived from the label)
  - toolbar tools for the new label (Q14; follow-up only if users notice)
  - editing or deleting relation definitions

## Approved plan

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[+ → Create new] --> B[Blueprint dialog: Label, Complement · Source → Target]
  B -- Continue --> C{validateNewRelationType}
  C -- invalid --> B
  C -- ok --> D[createTripletForPair from ENG-2243]
  D --> E[toasts: Relation type created · Discourse relation added]
  E --> F[back to type list with new type]
```

- **New dialog component (Blueprint `Dialog`).**
  - Title "Add relation type". Label and Complement inputs. The pair (`Source → Target`) shown as context (Q9). Cancel and Continue buttons.
  - The pending relation must survive the dialog. Clicks inside the dialog's portal fall outside `dropdownRef`, so suppress click-outside dismissal while the dialog is open.
  - Escape closes only the dialog. Remember that Escape in a popover inside a Blueprint Dialog closes the Dialog.
- **`validateNewRelationType(input, allTriplets, pair)`** (pure). Trim the inputs, then:
  1. Label and complement are required.
  2. Same label and complement as an existing triplet on any pair: reject with a pointer to `Add existing…`.
  3. Label exists with a **different** complement on any pair: **block** with "A relation called X already exists with complement Y".
  4. Label or complement equals a directional label the pair already shows: reject.
  - Rules 2–4 compare **case-insensitively** (Q5).
- **Submit:**
  - Call `createTripletForPair` unchanged. Errors use its toast and keep the dialog open.
  - Then show two toasts: "Relation type created", then "Discourse relation added" with the description "<label> added for <Source> and <Target>".
  - Return to the type list with the new type in it.
- **Wiring:** `DragHandleOverlay` passes `onCreateNew` only when stored relations are on.
- **Tests:** unit tests for each validation rule, including case-insensitive matching; submit with `createRelationSchema` mocked.
- **Live check (`dg-roam-load-extension`):**
  - DES-349 Cases 1, 2 and 3 end to end. Draw with the new type and confirm the stored relation block.
  - New label color: a custom label gets `COLOR_ARRAY[0]`, as expected.

ship_when_verified: no

## Key decisions
- **[2026-10-12] Block a label that exists with a different complement.** *Why:* the canvas groups triplets by label everywhere. The code that does this is in the overview's table:
  - `Tldraw.tsx:761-776` and `Export.tsx:360` build the label-keyed map.
  - `relationCreation.ts:95-112` dedupes options by directional label.
  - `DiscourseRelationUtil.tsx:1814-1848` resolves the triplet by label.
  - `getRelationColor` colors by label.
  - `DiscourseRelationTool.tsx:356` looks up the toolbar tool by label.
  - *Revisit if:* the canvas is changed to group by label + complement.
- **[2026-10-12] Case-insensitive validation only (Q5).** Block "supports" when "Supports" exists. The picker and the canvas stay exact-case.
- **[2026-10-12] No color picker.** The ticket is the source of truth over the mockup; color is derived from the label.
- **[2026-10-12] ENG-2245 is folded in.** DES-349 Case 2 is one flow.

## Gotchas / landmines
- **`getRelationColor` with no index gives every custom label `COLOR_ARRAY[0]`.** That's expected, not a bug in this PR.
- **The relation lookups that rule 2 mirrors are exact-case.** Check `checkConnectionTypeAcrossLabel` before assuming otherwise.
- **The save-path fix from ENG-2243 must already be on the branch.** Without it, a type created here can be saved under the wrong triplet.
- **Line refs are from eng-1955 at `f7d9f4a3`.** Re-grep before relying on them. `~/roam-ext-dev` is shared across worktrees.

## Current state
Planned, not started. Blocked on the ENG-2243 branch.

## Next step
Run `/start eng-2244`. Branch the worktree from `eng-2243-add-an-existing-discourse-relation-from-relation-menu`. Build the validation with its tests first, then the dialog.

## Open questions / blockers
- None open. All design questions were settled on 2026-10-12.

Setup is done, and I didn't start a dev server, as you asked.

**ENG-2244: Create a discourse relation from canvas and associate it with the selected node type pair**

- **Branch:** `eng-2244-create-a-discourse-relation-from-canvas-and-associate-it`, in `.claude/worktrees/eng-2244-…`
- **Base:** the worktree started from `origin/main`, but your saved plan says to stack this PR on ENG-2243. None of the stack has merged, so I reset the branch onto the local `eng-2243-add-an-existing-discourse-relation-from-relation-menu` (`634c424e`). It had no commits of its own, so nothing was lost. I ran `pnpm install` again afterwards.
- **ENG-2243 isn't on the remote.** It's still a local branch, so it will need pushing before this PR can target it.
- **Env files copied:** `skills/.env`, `packages/database/.env` (plus `.env.production` and `.env.branch`), `packages/database/supabase/functions/.env`, `apps/website/.env`, `apps/roam/.env`, `apps/obsidian/.env` (plus `.env.branch` and `.env.bak-eng2114`).
- **Skills:** all 8 `dg-*` skills are linked in `.claude/skills` and each one resolves to its `SKILL.md`.
- **Obsidian vault:** none leased, because the ticket only touches `apps/roam`.

**The ticket:** `Create new` in the canvas relation menu opens a dialog with Label and Complement fields. Color is assigned automatically. Submitting creates the relation and associates it with the active node-type pair. The new type shows up in the relation type menu without a page refresh, and two toasts appear: "Relation type created" and "Discourse relation added".

**Saved context (2026-10-12):**
- **TL;DR:** This is PR 3 of 3, stacked on ENG-2243, and it also covers ENG-2245 (Duplicate). The plan is a Blueprint dialog with no color picker. Input is checked against the existing triplets:
  - Label and complement are both required.
  - An exact duplicate of an existing type is rejected, with a pointer to `Add existing…`.
  - A label that already exists with a different complement is blocked.
  - A label that clashes with one this pair already shows is rejected.
  - The duplicate and clash checks ignore case.
  - Submit calls ENG-2243's `createTripletForPair`.
- **Next step:** build `validateNewRelationType` with its tests first, then the dialog, then wire `onCreateNew` in `DragHandleOverlay`.
- **Line numbers:** the line references in that context come from an older commit (`f7d9f4a3`), so I'll re-check them in the code before relying on them.

It returns an error message, or `null` when the input is valid. It trims both fields, and every comparison ignores case. The checks run in this order:

1. **Required:** label and complement must both be filled in.
2. **Already shown for this pair:** if the label or complement matches a label the pair already shows, it's rejected.
3. **Exact duplicate:** if the same label and complement exist on any pair, the message tells the user to use Add existing instead.
4. **Same label, different complement:** this is blocked with "A relation called X already exists with complement Y".

Two changes from the saved plan:

- **Check order:** the "already shown for this pair" check runs second instead of last. When a type is both shown on this pair and exists elsewhere, the more specific message wins.
- **Pair argument:** the function takes `shownLabels`, the same input `deriveRelationTypes` uses, instead of the pair itself. That keeps the messages generic ("these node types"), so the function doesn't need to look up node-type names.

**Imported types:** a not-yet-accepted imported type that exactly matches the input is let through on purpose. Add existing hides those, so pointing the user there would be a dead end, and saving accepts the matching type instead of creating a duplicate.

**Decision for you:** the plan only blocks a label that's already used. A new **complement** that matches an existing label or complement still gets through. Yes, it would stop users from typing a reverse by hand, but the reverse they'd type is exactly what causes the problem.

**Example:** "supports / is supported by" exists for Evidence → Claim. The user drags Claim → Evidence and types label "is supported by", complement "supports".

- **Today:** none of the four checks catch this, so it saves as a second relation type with the label and complement swapped.
- **With the complement check:** the complement "supports" matches an existing label, so it's blocked.

**Why blocking is right:** the canvas tells relation types apart by the label it shows for the drag direction. That swapped type would show "supports" one way and "is supported by" the other, the same as the original. If both types apply to a pair, the menu drops one of the duplicate labels. Drawing the shared label could then save the relation under the wrong one, which is the same collision the label check exists to prevent.

**How users still get the reverse:**

- **The type is already on this pair:** its complement already shows when dragging the other way, so nothing new is needed. The existing "already shown for this pair" check rejects the swapped spelling here today.
- **The type exists only on other pairs:** drag in the other direction (Evidence → Claim) and pick it from Add existing. In [DragHandleOverlay.tsx:294](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/overlays/DragHandleOverlay.tsx:294), Add existing always saves in the direction of the drag, so the drag direction is how users choose the direction.

So the check doesn't remove any capability. It removes a second, colliding way of saying the same thing. The catch is the error message: it should tell users how to get the reverse, not just say no. Something like:

> "supports" already exists as a relation. To add it the other way round, drag from Evidence to Claim and choose Add existing.

That's slightly broader than what I proposed earlier. It would check the new label and the new complement against all existing labels and complements, not only complement against complement. That's the same set of checks Obsidian runs when relation types are edited in its settings. Should I add it that way?

# DG Roam Load Extension

Use this skill for one complete lifecycle: build `apps/roam`, open an authenticated slot, register `apps/roam/dist`, activate it, verify DG runtime readiness, run an optional caller test, capture proof, and close.

It composes with `dg-roam-playwright-session` for account/profile selection.

## Quick Start

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1
```

Use another slot for isolated work:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 2
```

The script builds by default, verifies `window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder`, checks the DG settings UI, and writes proof under `local/roam-playwright/artifacts`.

To add feature-specific assertions without copying the loader, pass an ESM test module:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1 --test-module ./local/roam-playwright/feature-proof.mjs
```

```js
export default {
  readySelector: "[data-testid='feature-ready']",
  async ready({ page }) {
    return page.evaluate(() => Boolean(window.myFeature?.ready));
  },
  async run({ page, outDir }) {
    await page.getByText("Expected output").waitFor();
    return { assertion: "passed" };
  },
  async cleanup({ page, state }) {
    // Remove only fixtures created by run().
  },
};
```

`run()` starts only after the standard DG runtime proof and any caller readiness hook succeeds. `cleanup()` runs when `run()` started, including after a failed assertion. Return JSON-serializable proof values.

## Options

- `--slot 1|2|3`: Select the Roam account/profile.
- `--skip-build`: Load the existing `apps/roam/dist` without rebuilding.
- `--headed`: Run with a visible Chromium window.
- `--keep-open`: Leave the browser open after loading.
- `--dist <path>`: Load a different Roam extension folder. Use only when intentionally testing another build output.
- `--registration-name <name>`: Developer Extensions row name. Defaults to the built folder name, usually `dist`.
- `--test-module <path>`: Caller readiness, test, and cleanup hooks. Absolute Windows paths and paths containing spaces are supported.
- `--out <path>` and `--screenshot-name <name>`: Proof artifact locations.
- `--timeout <ms>`: UI and readiness timeout. Defaults to `45000`.

## Folder Loading

Roam Depot's folder button calls `window.showDirectoryPicker()`, not an `<input type="file">`. The script installs a temporary in-page directory-picker shim backed by the files in `apps/roam/dist`.

The loader uses native Playwright clicks for developer mode and folder controls. It treats the extension row as registration only, then clicks the header or row refresh control when present and waits for DG runtime proof. Roam versions that activate automatically may expose no refresh control.

An IndexedDB clone warning for the fake directory handle is expected and classified separately. Other page exceptions fail the run. `last-run.json` includes phase timings and bounded browser diagnostics; failures also capture a dedicated screenshot and compact DOM state.

## Safety Notes

- Do not commit `.env`, browser profiles, or artifacts.
- Do not commit real Roam test account emails, graph names, graph URLs, or proof screenshots.
- Keep feature fixtures, command interactions, and assertions in the caller module. Do not add them to the generic loader.
- Do not change Supabase local/branch/production config as part of this skill.
- Do not run production-backend smoke tests in this workflow.

Three things block `pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension --test-module` from driving the Roam tldraw canvas. All three fail *silently* as clean false negatives, not errors.

1. **`window.tldrawApps[pageTitle]` is the editor handle, but only in a dev build.** `apps/roam/scripts/build.ts` defaults `NODE_ENV` to `production`, which compiles the registration out entirely (`grep -c tldrawApps dist/extension.js` → 0). Build with `NODE_ENV=development npx tsx scripts/build.ts`, run the loader with `--skip-build`, then rebuild production afterwards so the worktree's `dist` is not left a dev artifact.
2. **The loader leaves the Roam settings dialog open** after its DG proof step. Every canvas click lands on the modal overlay instead. Press Escape until `.bp3-dialog, .bp3-overlay-open` is gone, in `ready()` *and* after the canvas mounts.
3. **Centre the camera per shape before clicking.** `zoomToFit()` across a row of fixtures puts the outer ones off-canvas or under the style panel; `editor.setCamera({x: -midX + 400, y: -midY + 300, z: 1})` makes every click land.

Always make the probe prove the menu opened before judging its contents — assert tldraw's own entries (`Duplicate|Delete|Copy as|Export as|Select all`) are present, else "menu did not open" scores as "menu without the item you're testing". A locked shape gets a reduced menu (no Duplicate/Delete), so include `Export as|Select all` in that marker.

Canvas pages are pages whose title matches `DEFAULT_CANVAS_PAGE_FORMAT` (`Canvas/*`), so a test module can make one with `roamAlphaAPI.data.page.create` and open it.

`pr-evidence` and `dg-roam-playwright-session` use a per-worktree profile, `<worktree>/local/roam-playwright/profiles/playwright-<slot>`. Every new worktree starts signed out. `apps/roam/.env` sets `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_AUTO_LOGIN=false`, so the stored credentials aren't used. Don't override that.

**Fix:** the user runs `pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/roam playwright:open -- --slot 1 --headed --allow-login` and signs in. It succeeds only when the output ends with `"ok": true, "configuredGraphLoaded": true`. Check that the profile's `Default/Cookies` mtime moved before retrying an upload.

**Dead end:** uploading through the user's signed-in Chrome with the claude-in-chrome tools works (hidden file input plus `roamAlphaAPI.file.upload`). But the tool blocks returning the Firebase URLs, which carry tokens in the query string, so the table can't reach the PR that way.

Seen on 2026-09-27 (ENG-2273): 3 of 18 blocks written that way ended up as bare captions, with the image gone. After uploading, re-read the blocks through the Playwright session, and `curl` every URL for `200 image/png`.

content.text:
I fixed the Cancel styling, and I checked it live in Roam: it's now a normal gray Blueprint button next to the blue Continue.

**Cause:** another extension in the test graph injects a CSS rule, most likely SmartBlocks, since its selectors mention `#smartblocks-prompt`. The rule targets `.roamjs-canvas-dialog .bp3-dialog-footer button:first-of-type` and paints that button light blue with white text. My dialog had borrowed the `roamjs-canvas-dialog` class from ConvertToDialog, and Cancel is its first footer button. The rule isn't in this repo or in our bundle.

**Fix:** I removed `roamjs-canvas-dialog` from the dialog's class list in [CreateRelationTypeDialog.tsx](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/overlays/CreateRelationTypeDialog.tsx) and left a one-line comment saying why. The dialog didn't need what that class gives: its inputs are already full width, and Blueprint's own focus outline still applies.

**Live check:** I opened the dialog again in Roam and read the computed styles. Cancel is now `rgb(245, 248, 250)` with dark text, before and after submitting. Continue is unchanged. The probe cleaned up its test pages and switched stored relations back off. The dialog and dropdown tests (35) pass, and typecheck, lint and Prettier are clean.

**Other dialogs:** three of them still use this class: `ModifyNodeDialog`, `CreateRelationDialog` and `SelectDialog`. ModifyNodeDialog already avoids the problem by putting Confirm first in the DOM and reversing the row. `CreateRelationDialog` has the same Cancel-then-primary order as mine, so it's probably affected in graphs with that extension. That's outside this ticket and I haven't changed it. I can flag it as a separate task if you want.

# Create PR

Work the phases in order. Phases 1-3 change the diff, and the body describes the final diff.
Any commit after Phase 1 starts makes earlier results stale: go back to Phase 1 and run every
later phase again on the new `HEAD`. Results from before this invocation, including manual
runs of the same skills, never count.

`ARGUMENTS`:

- `--dry-run`: run phases 0-5, print the title and body, stop. No push, no `gh pr create`.
- A base branch name. Otherwise infer it: if this branch was built on another open PR's
  branch, target that branch and say so in the body; else `main`.

## Phase 0: Load context

```bash
eval "$(bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve)"
awk '/^## Approved plan/{f=1;print;next} /^## /{f=0} f' "$CONTEXT_FILE"
```

The `## Approved plan` section holds a Mermaid diagram, intent per file or module, and a
`ship_when_verified: yes|no` line. If the file or section is missing, warn the user, skip
Phase 4, and treat `ship_when_verified` as `no`.

Set `BASE` (from `ARGUMENTS` or the stacked-branch inference above) before Phase 1.

## Phase 1: Comment audit

Only comments added on this branch. Never rewrite comments from committed work.

```bash
git diff "$BASE"...HEAD | grep -nE '^\+\s*(//|/\*|\*|\{/\*)'
```

For each added comment:

- It explains a workaround: fix the root cause, or delete the comment.
- Otherwise keep it only if it states a constraint the code cannot express (a platform
  quirk, a cross-file invariant, a choice a reader would "fix"), in two lines at most.
- Delete everything else: restatements, narration, banners, stale comments.

## Phase 2: Checks

From the worktree root (`$WORKTREE`):

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm ci:validate
git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "$BASE"...HEAD | xargs npx prettier --check
git diff --numstat "$BASE"...HEAD -- . ':!pnpm-lock.yaml' ':!**/package-lock.json' \
  | awk '{s+=$1+$2} END {print s}'
```

- Resolve every `ci:validate` and prettier failure.
- Over ~500 changed lines: warn the user and justify the coupling in the reviewer brief.
- Re-runs only (a PR already exists for this branch): block while any bot review thread is

gh api graphql -F owner=DiscourseGraphs -F repo=discourse-graph -F pr="$PR" -f query='
query($owner:String!,$repo:String!,$pr:Int!){repository(owner:$owner,name:$repo){

# Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
- Distinguish mandatory rules from preferences. Words such as “prefer” and “ideally,” the 200-line target, and the five-file guideline need judgment. Above 400 changed lines, excluding tests, check for the required explanation and review guide rather than rejecting the size alone.
- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. # Style Guide

This document outlines the coding standards and best practices for contributing to Discourse Graphs.

## TypeScript Guidelines

- Prefer `type` over `interface`
- Use explicit return types for functions
- Avoid `any` types when possible
- Prefer arrow functions over regular function declarations
- Use named parameters (object destructuring) when a function has more than 2 parameters

## UI Guidelines

- Use [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) for styling where possible
- When refactoring inline styles, use Tailwind classes.
- Use platform-native UI components first ([blueprintjs for Roam](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/developer-documentation/page/5BB8h4I7b), [Lucide icons for Obsidian](https://help.obsidian.md/Contributing+to+Obsidian/Style+guide), etc), with [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) as a fallback
- Maintain visual consistency with the host application's design system
- Follow responsive design principles
- Use `text-red-700` for Roam error message text. Obsidian keeps `text-error`; website and shared UI keep `text-destructive`. This convention does not change danger buttons, borders, backgrounds, or diagram colors.

## Code Formatting

- Use Prettier with the project's configuration
- Maintain consistent naming conventions:
  - PascalCase for components and types
  - camelCase for variables and functions
  - UPPERCASE for constants

## Code comments

Ask: **What would a maintainer get wrong if this comment were removed?** If there is no specific answer, remove it.

Keep comments that explain non-obvious decisions, external API or data constraints, known limitations, side effects, or ordering requirements. Prefer descriptive names when they can convey the same information.

Before keeping a comment, check:

- **Necessary:** Would removing it hide information needed to safely change or use the code?
- **Accurate:** Does it match what the code actually does, including relevant limitations and exceptions?
- **Concise:** Can it be shortened without losing necessary information?
- **Durable:** Will it still matter after this PR merges?
- **Local:** Is it next to the code that depends on the information?

Prefer one or two short sentences. Use longer explanations or examples when the constraint requires them; this is not a hard length limit.

Do not restate function names, types, test names, assertions, or obvious operations. Do not repeat an explanation already documented at its source; link to it when needed.

Put implementation history, review iterations, scope justifications, and ticket splits in inline GitHub comments. Keep durable constraints and known limitations in code or linked documentation. Link to the decision when describing behavior as agreed or accepted.

Agents must check added and modified comments against these criteria before handoff. Authors must review them manually before requesting review.

## Code Organization

- Prefer small, focused functions over inline code
- Co-locate code with its primary usage. Export it only for a concrete reuse need.
- Move code to `/utils` when it is shared across multiple call sites. Consider a shared package only after the code has stabilized and proven broadly reusable.
- Ground code movement in a current use case. Moving code because it feels cleaner adds churn without a clear functional benefit.
- Extract complex logic into well-named functions
- Prefer early returns over nested conditionals for better readability
- Function names should describe their purpose clearly:

```typescript
// ❌ Unclear and inline
const result = items.filter(
  (x) => x.date > now && x.status === "active" && !x.isArchived,
);

// ✅ Clear and reusable
const getActiveUnarchivedItems = (items: Item[]) => {
  return items.filter(isActiveAndUnarchived);
};

const isActiveAndUnarchived = (item: Item) => {
  return item.date > now && item.status === "active" && !item.isArchived;
};
```

- Choose descriptive function names that make comments unnecessary:

```typescript
  // ❌ Needs a comment to explain
  // Check if user can access premium features
  const check = (user: User) => { ... }

  // ✅ Self-documenting function name
  const hasValidPremiumSubscription = (user: User) => { ... }
```

- Break down complex operations into smaller, meaningful functions:

```typescript
// ❌ Large, multi-purpose function
const processData = (data: Data) => {
  // 30 lines of validation
  // 20 lines of transformation
  // 15 lines of formatting
};

// ✅ Composed of focused functions
const processData = (data: Data) => {
  const validatedData = validateDataFormat(data);
  const transformedData = transformToDesiredFormat(validatedData);
  return formatForDisplay(transformedData);
};
```

## Documentation

- Use sentence case by default in docs and UI copy. Capitalize official product/plugin names and exact UI labels, buttons, or page titles, but keep generic feature terms lowercase.

## Code hygiene

- Remove unused imports, temporary comments, and debug logging before requesting review. Preserve intentional operational logging.
- Handle errors gracefully and log enough context to diagnose failures without exposing credentials or sensitive data.

## Testing

- Write unit tests for new functionality
- Ensure tests are meaningful and maintainable
- Cover relevant edge cases, error paths, and alternative flows.
- Expose workspace unit tests through a `test:unit` script so the root validation command includes them.
# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.

# Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

For a name inherited from `Object.prototype`, the grouping code mistakes the inherited value for an existing array and calls `.push` on it. This throws after persistence, so retrying the dialog encounters a saved duplicate rather than repairing the canvas.
**Example:** Enter label `constructor`, complement `is constructed by`, and click Continue. The block is saved; grouping sees the inherited `constructor` function and throws instead of listing the new type.
**Recommended fix:** Change `groupRelationsByLabel` to use an own-property check or a null-prototype accumulator, so arbitrary user labels work. Add a regression test using `constructor` and `toString`.

Learn more
The validator permits one exact provisional schema on the selected pair because [createTripletForPair](https://github.com/discoursegraphs/discourse-graph/blob/1b488ea034516a4ce7ea2701da582d93f1cf227d/apps/roam/src/components/canvas/existingRelationTypes.ts#L170-L184 "apps/roam/src/components/canvas/existingRelationTypes.ts:170-184") accepts that schema on save. But `isAcceptedOnSave` is a boolean, and the duplicate predicate skips every schema with that text, including accepted schemas on unrelated pairs. The save then accepts a redundant imported schema even though the existing picker offers the accepted type.
**Example:** An imported provisional `supports / is supported by` exists on Evidence → Claim, and an accepted identical type exists on Question → Hypothesis. Creating the type on Evidence → Claim passes validation and accepts the imported schema, leaving two accepted versions of the same type.
**Recommended fix:** Exempt only the exact provisional schema on the selected pair from duplicate detection. Keep accepted matches, and other provisional matches, eligible for the duplicate error.

Learn more
A stored relation has a label for its forward direction and a complement for its reverse direction. For a same-type pair with identical label and complement, both direction checks match a query by name and node type. [getFilteredRelations](https://github.com/discoursegraphs/discourse-graph/blob/1b488ea034516a4ce7ea2701da582d93f1cf227d/apps/roam/src/utils/registerDiscourseDatalogTranslators.ts#L379-L394 "apps/roam/src/utils/registerDiscourseDatalogTranslators.ts:379-394") returns the forward result first, so the reverse schema-ID and endpoint clauses are never generated for the same name.
**Example:** Create `related / related` between Claim and Claim and store a relation from Claim A to Claim B. Querying for claims `related` to B from the opposite direction misses the expected inverse match.
**Recommended fix:** Reject identical label/complement names in `validateNewRelationType`, or update the query translator to preserve both matching directions for the same schema.

I fixed three of Devin's four findings, pushed them to the PR as `aa536a77`, replied in those three threads and resolved them. I left the fourth unchanged because it isn't a bug. All 69 test files (673 tests) and `ci:validate` pass, and the new tests fail on the old code.

**What the dialog now rejects:**
- **Reserved query condition names**, such as `is a`, `self` or `Has Any Relation To`, ignoring case. Each relation name is registered as a query condition, so saving one of these would silently change what existing queries do. Names that already belong to a relation type are still allowed. To get the list of names, I added a small `getConditionKeys` export in `conditionToDatalog.ts`.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/pr-evidence

# PR evidence upload

Uploads PNGs through `roamAlphaAPI.file.upload` in an authenticated Roam Playwright slot, files them under a page in the slot's graph (`discourse-dev-graph`), and emits a Markdown table that create-pr pastes into the Evidence section.

## When to use

- After verification (Roam `load-extension` run, Obsidian CDP run, manual captures) left PNGs on disk.
- Before create-pr builds the body. Roam PRs: reuse the verification's slot once that run has closed. Obsidian PRs: omit `--slot`.

## Command

Run from the worktree root, using the worktree's own `tsx` so the relative PNG paths and the repo's Playwright resolve:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts \
  [--slot N] [--branch <b>] [--label "<YYYY-MM-DD · shortsha · harness>"] [--harness <name>] \
  [--out table.md] [--settle-ms 5000] \
  shot1.png="Empty state" shot2.png="After import" ...
```

- `pnpm --filter roam exec tsx ...` also works, but it changes cwd to `apps/roam`, so pass absolute PNG paths.
- `--branch` defaults to the current git branch. `--label` defaults to `<today> · <short sha> · <--harness or "manual">`.
- Caption defaults to the file name without extension.
- No `--slot`: tries each configured slot (1, 2, 3) and moves on only on a profile-lock error.
- Headless by default (`HEADLESS=false` to watch).

## Output contract

- stdout: JSON `{page, pageUid, branchBlockUid, runBlockUid, items: [{caption, url, blockUid}]}`.
- stderr: `Markdown table: <path>`. The file defaults to `pr-evidence-<runBlockUid>.md` next to the first PNG and contains `| Scenario | Screenshot |` rows with `![caption](url)`. create-pr pastes it as-is.
- URLs are public Firebase storage links (`200 image/png` without cookies, verified 2026-09-23).

## Roam structure

```
Trang test/                       (page, found or created)
  <branch>                        (top-level block, reused on every run)
    <date · sha · harness>        (new run block per invocation, appended last)
      <caption> ![](<url>)        (one per PNG)
```

## Gotchas

- Imports `apps/roam/scripts/playwright/roamSession.ts` from the current worktree (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), so profiles live in that worktree's `local/roam-playwright/profiles/` unless `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PROFILE_DIR_<n>` is set.
- A slot's profile can only be open once. Close the verification session first, never delete lock files.
- Login errors (expired session, 2FA) come from `openRoamSession`; recover with `pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot N --headed --allow-login`, then rerun.
- Never print values from `apps/roam/.env`.
- Uploads cannot be rolled back and Roam cannot list graph files, so don't loop retries on a failing run.
- tsx injects `__name()` into functions passed to `page.evaluate`; the script shims it in the page first. Keep that shim if you edit the in-page code.

# Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

## Resolve the evidence

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
- Distinguish mandatory rules from preferences. Words such as “prefer” and “ideally,” the 200-line target, and the five-file guideline need judgment. Above 400 changed lines, excluding tests, check for the required explanation and review guide rather than rejecting the size alone.
- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. Do not invent exceptions, team approval, testing outcomes, or video contents. If a required document is unavailable or rules conflict without a clear applicable resolution, report the gap instead of guessing.
- Respect workflow timing: missing Loom or review evidence can be reported as outstanding before requesting review while a draft is being prepared. Do not call future post-merge steps violations on an open PR.
- Keep scope expansions in Scope check. Verification is optional. Standards check only records whether the check ran.

## Return the result

Return a copy-ready section:

```markdown
## Standards check

- [x] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.
```

The checkbox means the review ran, not that all requirements passed. If the diff cannot be resolved or the review could not run, leave it unchecked and tell the author what blocked it. Separately make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them; do not require these details in the PR body. Rerun affected checks after changes to code, rules, or PR metadata.

content.text:
I've updated the body of [DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1557](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1557).

**Code fix pushed first.** Before editing the body, I pushed `05ea020e` (the option you chose). The name check had been comparing against every registered query condition, which gave two bugs:
- The name of a relation type deleted earlier in the session stayed blocked until Roam reloaded.
- A built-in name could get through if an incomplete relation already used it.

It now checks only against the built-in conditions. A new unit test covers the second case.

**What changed in the body:**
- **Verification:** a second table for the Chrome run at `aa536a77`. It covers the reserved query name, `constructor`, imported and accepted duplicates, the Add existing hint, the `?` placeholder, the same-type pair, Escape, and creating and drawing a type.
- **Screenshots:** both are uploaded with `pr-evidence`, and their URLs return `200 image/png`. One shows both toasts with the new type listed; the other shows the same-type rejection.
- **Review focus:** now mentions the new rejections.
- **Scope check:** now lists the new rejections and the `builtIn` flag on the query-condition registry, which spans `conditionToDatalog.ts` and `registerDiscourseDatalogTranslators.ts`.
- **Not verified:** the `05ea020e` fix wasn't run live, only in unit tests. The close button hiding while saving couldn't be observed. Accepting an exact imported triplet on its own pair is unit-tested only, because the test graph has no such triplet.

**Checks on `05ea020e`:** the delegated review found nothing, and scope-check and the standards check also ran on this commit. All 69 test files (674 tests) and `ci:validate` pass.

The diff is now 6 non-test files and 313 lines. That's under the 400-line limit but one file over the "fewer than five" guideline; the extra file is the five-line flag in `registerDiscourseDatalogTranslators.ts`.

**Still outstanding:** the Loom video, and a comment on ENG-2244 recording the decision to validate new names. The "Imported pair hides an accepted duplicate" thread from Devin is still unanswered and unresolved; my draft reply is in the earlier message if you want to post it.

That message is expected while **stored relations are off**, and they're off in `discourse-dev-graph` right now: my test cleanup switched them back off, as agreed. The build isn't the problem.

The toast comes from [DragHandleOverlay.tsx:224-233](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/overlays/DragHandleOverlay.tsx:224). When you drag between two nodes:

- **Stored relations off, no types for the pair:** you get the toast "No relation types are defined between these node types", and no menu opens.
- **Stored relations on:** the menu always opens. With no types for the pair, it shows the empty state with **Add existing…** and **Create new**.

This gate comes from the base branch (ENG-2243), not from this PR. Legacy mode drops triplets that have no if-conditions, so a type added from the canvas would never appear, and the menu actions stay hidden.

**To see the new dialog:**
1. Open **DG: Open - Discourse settings** → **Enable stored relations**, and choose **Reactivate without Migration**. That only flips the setting; "Activate and Migrate" would also migrate the graph's relations.
2. Refresh the developer extension (or reload the page), so the 13:59 build loads.
3. Drag between two nodes whose pair has no relation types. The menu should show Add existing… and Create new.

If you're testing in a different graph where stored relations are already on and you still get that toast, tell me which graph. In that case something else is wrong.

content.text:
Relation arrows no longer default to white: new custom types now draw in grey, which I checked in Chrome on light and dark canvases. Added types keep their named color, matched ignoring case, so `supports` is green. The fix is pushed to [DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1557](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1557) (head `06898ef6`), and the PR body is updated.

**Why everything was white:** Roam doesn't store a color per relation type. `getRelationColor(label)` gives named colors only to exact-case `Supports`, `Opposes` and `Informs` and their complements. Every other label fell back to white. Arrows also paint that name straight into the SVG stroke as a CSS color, so tldraw's theme palette never applies. That's why tldraw's "black" stayed black in dark mode. This affected every path that draws a custom relation, not just this ticket's.

**What changed** in `getRelationColor`:
- **Named colors match ignoring case.**
- **Every other label falls back to grey instead of white.** Grey is the only color that's both a valid CSS color and readable on light and dark canvases. Its one drawback: custom types now share their color with `Informs`, which is also grey.
- **Toolbar and tool-panel colors are unchanged,** apart from positions past the end of the palette, which now wrap instead of breaking.
- **Existing arrows keep their stored color.** Only newly drawn ones change.
- **Paths affected:** the drag-handle menu, the toolbar relation tool, the style panel and the legacy arrow migration.

**A mistake I made and reverted:** in the first version (`8998af24`) I also removed white from the toolbar palette. The review caught that this shifted every toolbar and tool-panel color, and pushed `light-red` into the relation shape's default color. `light-red` isn't a valid CSS color, so arrows using it would render without a line. `06898ef6` restores the palette exactly. One side effect: the toolbar's first custom relation icon is white again, as it was before this PR.

**Checks on `06898ef6`:**
- 70 test files (677 tests), typecheck and `ci:validate` pass. The new color tests fail on the old function.
- The delegated review found nothing.
- Scope-check and the standards check also ran.
- In Chrome, I drew with a new type and with an added named type, then reviewed the tool panel and dark mode. That was on `8998af24`. The palette fix afterwards doesn't affect arrows drawn from the menu, and unit tests cover it.
- I deleted the test data, including the `supports` triplet my Add existing test created. I left stored relations on and didn't touch your canvas.

**Loading a new build into Roam:** reloading the page doesn't do it. Roam keeps its own copy of the developer extension until you refresh `dist` under Settings → Roam Depot → Developer Extensions. I'd guess that's also part of why you weren't seeing changes earlier. I saved this as a memory note.

**Decision for you: PR size.** The PR is now 7 non-test files and 348 lines, over the "fewer than five files" guideline. The color problem predates this ticket and affects the whole canvas, so a reviewer may ask to split it out. The case for keeping it here is that Done When needs an automatic, visible color. Your call.
